newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices track foreign markets up.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices track foreign markets up.

text.p: Danish bond prices followed foreign markets up on Tuesday with increased interest in government bonds and less in mortgage-backed paper.
"There is a very positive undertone to the market and the yield curve is a little flatter," a trader said.
At 1120 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 stood at 110.90, yielding 6.33 percent, up 0.40 point from Monday's close, in turnover of 1.3 billion crowns.
The seven percent 2007 bond traded at 103.46, yielding 6.52 percent, up from around 103.00 at close of business on Monday and with volume of around 1.4 billion crowns.
The 2006 benchmark's yield gap with Germany was 46 basis points, compared to Monday's 48 bp and the 2007 gap to the bund was also two basis points narrower, at 65 bp.
The 2006 bond's June future, expiring on June 16, was untraded at 110.34.
The crown was slightly firmer than on Monday, at 3.8075 per mark compared to 3.8079.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 was up 0.60 point to 98.30, in turnover of 230 million crowns. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
